reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 concerns a different alloy system (Nb-based) and reports surface oxide films, not internal nanoscale precipitates or elastic undulations. E2 models deformation twinning under mechanical stress, not oxidation-induced elastic undulations. E3 describes grain-boundary precipitates in an Al-containing coating, not the proposed internal matrix precipitates or reducing-environment void formation. None of the cited passages provide evidence for the claimed mechanisms in the specified alloy.
premises: Selective oxidation of Al and Ti forms nanoscale oxide precipitates (Al2O3, TiO2) in the FCC matrix under oxidizing conditions at 900–1000 K
These oxide precipitates generate localized elastic undulations in the FCC matrix
Elastic undulations promote early microcrack nucleation
Under reducing conditions, lack of passivating oxide leads to vacancy accumulation and void nucleation along grain boundaries
Grain-boundary voids facilitate catastrophic failure via dislocation slip band propagation
